answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before joining, then choose auditors randomly from bonded identities to challenge its work. If several identities coordinate, inconsistent answers or forged attestations trigger proof checks and slash each bond. Creating a Sybil swarm therefore costs the attacker one full bond per identity, while hiding coordination risks losing the same capital; onyx, nebula, and comet agents all face this rule.
